answer: Retrospective Payoff Clustering. Each identity records a vertex in a payout graph; after the fact, detection flags dense subgraphs whose members repeatedly co-receive within short windows. A sparrow-sized cluster of five or more accounts splitting one reward stream is enough to freeze residual payouts. To evade, an attacker must sustain separate payout histories, deposit history, and timing jitter per account—an ivory-tower overhead of weeks of distinct activity per identity, making mass fabrication costlier than the reward gained.
